chunk_findings.detail: The earlier probe does not answer this: sharing `W.git_paths(repo, "ls-files")` with doctor notes is not the same as rewriting the shared registry, and "doctor runs on primary == main" is false for a dirty index. Given main still has `api/setup.py` (the tree the bug measures with `git ls-tree main`) while the index has staged the split to `api/setup/`, `--fix-stale-globs` rewrites every open item that declares `api/setup.py` onto `api/setup/`. Those items then lease a path that does not exist on main and no longer cover `api/setup.py`, so overlap with tasks still on the module is invisible. The same `ls-files` source is now used by the new `_correct_stale_package_globs` in `ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim.py`, so a claim from that index persists the same wrong retarget.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py:_apply_stale_globs

chunk_findings.detail: The new claim-time correction uses `W.git_paths(repo, "ls-files")`, i.e. the current worktree’s index, not the tree the bug measures (`git ls-tree main`). The earlier HIGH against `health.py` was refuted only because doctor runs on the primary checkout/main tree; claim has no such invariant: `claim` runs in the repository/working tree the agent is currently in. Concrete failure: an agent claims from a feature branch created before a split, where `api/setup.py` still exists and `api/setup/` does not, while `main` has `api/setup/`. An open item declares `api/setup.py` (stale against main). `tracked` from that branch contains `api/setup.py` and no `api/setup/_core.py`, so `stale_package_globs` returns no stale result, `_correct_stale_package_globs` returns `want` unchanged, and `lz.globs` remains `api/setup.py`. The lease then covers none of `api/setup/` on main, so overlapping edits to `api/setup/_core.py` remain invisible. The correction should be based on the main tree for open-item globs, not the local index.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim.py:184 `_correct_stale_package_globs`

chunk_findings.detail: The fix rewrites the shared item registry from `W.git_paths(repo, "ls-files")`, i.e. the current index of `repo`, not the `git ls-tree main` tree the bug is measured against. `health()` accepts an arbitrary `repo` and never pins it to `main`; on a branch or dirty/staged index that has split `api/setup.py` into `api/setup/` while `main` still has the module, every open item declaring `api/setup.py` is rewritten to `api/setup/` and loses its lease on the file that still exists on `main`. The previous triage says doctor runs on the primary checkout and thus `ls-files` equals `main`, but nothing in this code enforces that, and the new mutation makes the wrong-tree choice destructive rather than merely cosmetic.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py:_apply_stale_globs

chunk_findings.detail: When `_items.update` returns `O.OK` but with nonempty `globs_withheld`, the requested rewrite is only partly applied, yet `_apply_stale_globs` appends a `notes` entry instead of a `problems` entry. The section's own contract says a stale glob the fix could not rewrite is a PROBLEM. A `ddflow doctor --fix-stale-globs` run can therefore exit successfully while an item remains only "partly corrected" and still has a stale package glob withheld, so a caller treating exit 0 as "all stale globs were rewritten" is wrong. Example: another live lease prevents the replacement package glob from being added; the code records `"globs partly corrected; withheld: ..."` and returns no problem.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py:_apply_stale_globs

chunk_findings.detail: `has_py_glob` is documented and used as “unfinished item declares a glob ending in `.py`”, but it iterates `st.items.values()` without excluding `i.removed`, `DONE`, or `ABANDONED`. A state whose only `.py` globs belong to a removed or already-closed item still returns `True`, so `health.py` calls `_tree_files(repo)`. If `_tree_files` then returns `None` because `git ls-tree` failed, the health report emits `"stale task globs not fixed: git could not list the tracked files"` even though there are no unfinished `.py` globs to fix. Concrete input: `st.items` contains one `DONE` item with globs `["ddflow/config.py"]` and no unfinished items; `_tree_files(repo)` returns `None`; report returns a stale-glob warning, which is wrong. Filter `has_py_glob` to the same live item set used by `stale_glob_updates`.

chunk_findings.detail: The fix rewrites the shared item registry from `W.git_paths(repo, "ls-files")`, i.e. the current index of `repo`, not the `git ls-tree main` tree the bug is measured against. `health()` accepts an arbitrary `repo` and never pins it to `main`; on a branch or dirty/staged index that has split `api/setup.py` into `api/setup/` while `main` still has the module, every open item declaring `api/setup.py` is rewritten to `api/setup/` and loses its lease on the file that still exists on `main`. The previous triage says doctor runs on the primary checkout and thus `ls-files` equals `main`, but nothing in this code enforces that, and the new mutation makes the wrong-tree choice destructive rather than merely cosmetic.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py:_apply_stale_globs

chunk_findings.detail: When `_items.update` returns `O.OK` but with nonempty `globs_withheld`, the requested rewrite is only partly applied, yet `_apply_stale_globs` appends a `notes` entry instead of a `problems` entry. The section's own contract says a stale glob the fix could not rewrite is a PROBLEM. A `ddflow doctor --fix-stale-globs` run can therefore exit successfully while an item remains only "partly corrected" and still has a stale package glob withheld, so a caller treating exit 0 as "all stale globs were rewritten" is wrong. Example: another live lease prevents the replacement package glob from being added; the code records `"globs partly corrected; withheld: ..."` and returns no problem.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health.py:_apply_stale_globs

chunk_findings.detail: `has_py_glob` is documented and used as “unfinished item declares a glob ending in `.py`”, but it iterates `st.items.values()` without excluding `i.removed`, `DONE`, or `ABANDONED`. A state whose only `.py` globs belong to a removed or already-closed item still returns `True`, so `health.py` calls `_tree_files(repo)`. If `_tree_files` then returns `None` because `git ls-tree` failed, the health report emits `"stale task globs not fixed: git could not list the tracked files"` even though there are no unfinished `.py` globs to fix. Concrete input: `st.items` contains one `DONE` item with globs `["ddflow/config.py"]` and no unfinished items; `_tree_files(repo)` returns `None`; report returns a stale-glob warning, which is wrong. Filter `has_py_glob` to the same live item set used by `stale_glob_updates`.
